notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET (cell is frozen, daemon=incapable — no recording is taken). Copilot CLI 1.0.77 genuinely streams: the 1.0.77 app.js carries assistant.message_start / message_delta / streaming_delta / reasoning_delta / tool_call_delta. NONE of them are persisted. The session event writer (app.js Wfe class) queues only selected events through a native recordEventJson filter and then flushes them DEBOUNCED (500/100 ms) as a BATCH of complete records via sessionEventsAppendLocal — so events.jsonl only ever gains whole JSON lines, in bursts. A live 5-session / 13-turn 1.0.77 corpus confirms it: exactly one complete assistant.message per assistant.turn_start-turn_end pair (including a 764-output-token long-prose reply), and zero message_delta/streaming_delta/message_start lines anywhere. The streaming_window phase below therefore has NO partial-flush window to assert over and a recording would only duplicate basic-turn. This spec is retained as the no-flicker ideal a recording WOULD validate should Copilot start persisting its delta family: one contiguous working→ready arc across the streamed turn, no premature ready before assistant.turn_end, no waiting. The copilot parser is already correct for that world — parseAssistantMessage (parser.go:189) never settles a turn and only assistant.turn_end maps to turn_done (parser.go:98-99), so partial flushes would sustain working; the gap is emission, not handling. The torn/partial-trailing-LINE reading of the scenario name is a shared-tailer property (large_line_test.go), not copilot-recordable; copilot's own ParseLine returns Skip=true for a line with no type field, so a torn record degrades to a skip. SESSION IDENTITY (were it recorded): the interactive REPL mints a transient proc-<PID> pre-session born ready before $COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl exists (it is not created until the first prompt), and the real <session-id> session appears under a DIFFERENT id — hence the two-phase birth below, with every later phase pinned to the real session via same_session_as. OBSERVATIONS: model is provisional, to be filled from a recording (Copilot resolves 'auto' to a concrete model via session.auto_mode_resolved); tokens/cost would be non-zero from per-message outputTokens, but input tokens land only at session.shutdown.
